nodes.label: Employee
nodes.summary: Asks a question in natural language and expects an answer that cites documents they are allowed to read.

nodes.label: Source systems
nodes.summary: Wikis, file stores, ticket systems and similar. They own the documents and their permissions.

nodes.label: LLM service
nodes.summary: Generates chunk context at ingestion and the final answer at query time. For serving internals see note 22.

nodes.label: Ingestion pipeline
nodes.summary: Turns documents into searchable chunks: change detection, chunking, optional context generation, embedding and indexing.

nodes.label: Sync and change detection
nodes.summary: Pulls new, changed and deleted documents and permission changes from the sources. Industry practice; neither source describes it.

nodes.label: Parser and chunker
nodes.summary: Extracts text and splits it into chunks. The RAG paper used disjoint 100-word chunks; Anthropic says chunks are usually no more than a few hundred tokens and that chunk size, boundaries and overlap affect retrieval.

nodes.label: Contextualizer
nodes.summary: Asks a model for a short (usually 50-100 tokens) explanation of how the chunk fits its document, prepended before embedding and keyword indexing.

nodes.label: Embedder
nodes.summary: Computes a dense vector per chunk with a document encoder (the RAG paper used a BERT-base bi-encoder).

nodes.label: Vector index
nodes.summary: Approximate nearest-neighbour index over chunk vectors. The RAG paper used FAISS with a Hierarchical Navigable Small World index over 21M chunks.

nodes.label: Keyword index (BM25)
nodes.summary: Lexical index over the contextualized chunks; finds exact identifiers and technical terms that embeddings can miss.

nodes.label: Chunk store
nodes.summary: Chunk text, source link, version and the access list. Needed to cite sources and filter by permission.

nodes.label: Query service
nodes.summary: Answers a question: applies the user's permission scope, retrieves from both indexes, reranks, builds the prompt and returns an answer with citations.

nodes.label: Permission scope
nodes.summary: Resolves who the user is and which documents they may read, and applies that as a filter inside retrieval. Industry practice.

nodes.label: Hybrid retriever
nodes.summary: Searches the vector index and the keyword index and merges the results into a candidate list (Anthropic used the top 150).

nodes.label: Reranker
nodes.summary: Scores each candidate against the question and keeps the top K (Anthropic used 20), improving results at the price of added latency and cost.

nodes.label: Prompt builder and citations
nodes.summary: Puts the chosen chunks in the prompt, instructs the model to answer from them and cite them, and returns the streamed answer.

nodes.label: Evaluation and feedback
nodes.summary: Logs question, retrieved chunks, answer and user feedback; runs labelled retrieval and answer tests before changes ship. Industry practice; Anthropic advises always running evals.

steps.caption: The question arrives with the user's identity; the service resolves which documents they may read.
The retriever receives the question together with the allowed scope.
It searches the vector index for chunks close in meaning.
It also searches the keyword index for exact terms.
The merged candidates (a wide list) go to the reranker.
The reranker keeps the top chunks.
The prompt contains the chunks and instructions to answer from them and cite them.
The answer is streamed back with citations.
The exchange is logged for evaluation and feedback.

flows.name: A document is added or changed

steps.caption: Sync detects a new or changed document.
It is parsed and split into chunks.
Each chunk goes to the contextualizer.
A model writes a short context for the chunk from the whole document.
The contextualized chunk is embedded.
The vector is written to the vector index.
The same text is added to the keyword index.

flows.name: A user's access is revoked (security failure to prevent)

steps.caption: Sync sees that a document is now restricted or deleted at the source.
The chunk store's access list is updated or the chunks are removed. Until this lands, queries could still return the chunks, so the delay is a leak window to keep small (our design reasoning).
At query time the retriever checks permissions against the store, so revoked chunks are no longer returned.
A query for a specific error code returns semantically similar but wrong chunks.
The keyword index matches the exact code and returns the right chunk, which the reranker can then promote.
